.
You’ll work alongside fellow “learn-it-all” builders who are passionate about their work and eager to collaborate, and you’ll help bring the broader People Analytics team along as we all learn to work in new ways.
This is not a traditional analyst role - you won’t be producing analyses or reports. Instead, you’ll use your analytical background to build the tools that let others get those answers themselves, and to be the voice of the analyst inside our team.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Build and extend our people-analytics MCP server: add new datasets, improve answer quality, and cut response times.
Diagnose and fix bugs across our AI tools, and test rigorously before things ship.
Partner across the People Analytics team to build and test GitHub Copilot skills that encode analytical methods.
Prototype new solutions as opportunities emerge across our workstreams, partnering with senior teammates and adapting quickly as priorities shift in a fast-moving, still-forming space.
Stay embedded with analysts: learn where the tools fall short and turn that feedback directly into improvements that people actually adopt.
Help others level up: share what you learn, teach new AI tools and techniques, and contribute to a growing skills community across the team.
Build responsibly with sensitive people data: bake confidentiality, access, and guardrails into what you ship, and handle governed data with strict adherence to privacy requirements and appropriate legal reviews.

Who We Are
With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility.
Who We Are
With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system — reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed, and flexibility.
What We Need
We are looking for a Senior Security Automation Engineer to join our Security Automation team within our Information Security organization. Your job will be to design and build AI-driven automations, internal applications, copilots, and agentic workflows that help Security, IT, GRC, and business teams operate more efficiently and securely — and to help build the guardrails that keep AI-driven actions safe, compliant, and trustworthy.
This is a hands-on, high-autonomy engineering role, not a prompt-writing job. You will take loosely defined problems and own them end to end{{:}} shape the requirements, choose the architecture, use modern AI development tools to build fast, personally validate the code you ship, and deliver production systems. You will be one of two engineers on a small, high-trust team inside the Security organization — your work will be visible from day one, and your first project supports a compliance goal set by our CIO and VP of Security.
What We Do
The Security Automation team is part of the Information Security organization, which protects Symbotic’s enterprise, systems, and operations by building secure, scalable capabilities that reduce risk and strengthen compliance. The team creates automation, integrations, and AI-powered workflows that support security operations, compliance activities (ISO 27001, SOC 2), access governance, endpoint compliance, shadow-IT discovery, vulnerability management, and broader operational efficiency across the business.
What You’ll Do
Design, develop, and maintain AI-driven automations, internal applications, copilots, and workflow orchestration solutions that improve how Security, IT, GRC, and business teams operate.
Build agentic workflows that can retrieve context, reason through tasks, use approved tools, and generate actionable outputs.
Automate repetitive security, compliance, and operational processes — user access reviews, software approval workflows, compliance evidence collection — to reduce manual effort and accelerate response times.
Integrate AI and automation workflows with enterprise platforms such as ITSM, IAM, SIEM, SOAR, GRC, ticketing, knowledge management, vulnerability management, and cloud security tools.
Develop secure human-in-the-loop approval patterns for high-risk, sensitive, or business-critical AI-driven actions.
Create reusable workflow patterns, prompts, templates, and service components that can be adopted across teams.
Partner with stakeholders across Security, IT, Engineering, Compliance, and the business to identify high-value automation opportunities and translate needs into practical technical solutions.
Contribute to penetration-testing and red-team efforts as our offensive security program grows.
Measure and report outcomes such as time saved, error reduction, throughput improvement, and risk reduction.
Help define standards, governance, and guardrails for the secure, responsible, and compliant use of AI across the organization.
What You’ll Need
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field. Two years of experience in parrot nerotrophiccs.
Minimum of 5 years of professional software engineering experience with genuine full-stack depth — client, server, and data/storage — and the DevOps skills (Docker, CI/CD, cloud) to run what you build.
Hands-on experience building with AI and LLM systems{{:}} LLM APIs, agent frameworks, RAG pipelines, prompt design, and AI-assisted development tools — including the judgment to review and validate AI-generated code before it ships.
Strong development skills, ideally Python, with API-driven integrations{{:}} REST APIs, webhooks, message queues, databases, and workflow orchestration platforms.
Experience building internal tools, automation workflows, or service integrations in enterprise environments.
Understanding secure system design{{:}} identity and access management, role-based access control, secrets management, and audit logging.
The autonomy to take an ambiguous business needs and deliver a working, documented, production system with minimal direction, plus strong communication skills across technical and non-technical teams.
Preferred Qualifications
Familiarity with enterprise security platforms{{:}} SIEM, SOAR, ITSM, IAM, GRC, vulnerability management, endpoint or cloud security.
Exposure compliance frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2) and control automation.
Interest or experience in penetration testing and red-team tooling.
TypeScript, Go, or Rust; PostgreSQL, SQLite, or BigQuery; infrastructure as code.
Our environment
Hybrid at our Wilmington, MA headquarters. No travel required.
About Symbotic
Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com.

Something you built, with or without AI, that you can walk us through line by line: a GitHub repo, a deployed app, a class project, or work from an internship or bootcamp.

America is critically deficient in production of defensive munitions- we currently produce shipborne interceptors in the few hundreds per year while our adversaries are producing offensive threats in the tens of thousands per year. Furientis was started to help solve this problem- introducing a new class of cost-effective, high production rate, interceptor missiles. We're seeking motivated individuals who internalize this problem and are eager to apply their past experience in similar industries (aerospace, defense, automotive/racing, robotics) and out of the box thinking to solve this problem for the US and its allies.
About The Team
The Seeker Team builds the eyes and the targeting logic of our weapon system: a low-cost, mass-producible, multimodal missile seeker that leans on commercial supply chains where they outperform, and vertically integrates wherever possible. On a modern missile, the seeker is 40 to 60% of unit cost and often drives overly long delivery cycles; accordingly, the seeker team is at the tip of the spear for delivering capability to our customers and value to the taxpayer.
Seeker design has exactly two real constraints: physics and mission. Nothing else is a show-stopper, only an obstacle to overcome. We are a small, deeply technical team that drives capability through ingenuity and bias for action and ships hardware that flies. This is a wear-many-hats environment where you must be comfortable "building the airplane in flight" and stepping well outside your comfort zone; a narrowly scoped role with clean handoffs is not what this team offers.
This is an AI-native team. Through fluent use of cutting-edge agentic coding tools, one engineer here consistently out-delivers a much larger conventional team. You will have opinions about where these tools help and where they do not, provide governance input, and build out an AI-centric workflow from day one.
About The Role
You will contribute to the production of perception and estimation algorithms at the core of our seeker: detection, tracking, classification, and aimpoint localization on infrared (IR) imagery and fused sensor measurements, against targets that fight back. As part of the Seeker Team, you will research, implement, optimize, and validate algorithms in these areas, including modern AI and machine learning (ML) methods where they earn their place. Runtime efficiency is a hard constraint: everything you build must run within a strict latency budget on embedded flight-compute hardware. You will work closely with the broader Seeker Team to carry your algorithms from first prototype into flight.
What You'll Do
Design and implement object detection algorithms for mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, robust to clutter, domain shift, and countermeasures.
Develop multi-object tracking and state estimation: filtering, data association, and line-of-sight estimates for missile guidance.
Implement track lifecycle management: initialization, maintenance, confirmation, and termination under real sensor conditions.
Develop segmentation, classification, and discrimination algorithms that separate targets from decoys, debris, and background.
Develop aimpoint localization and the associated image-processing methods that support terminal accuracy.
Contribute to perception-related sensor fusion, combining IR and X-band radar measurements into a consistent track picture.
Implement, optimize, and validate your algorithms for real-time flight: measured latency, covariance and confidence you can defend, and performance proven in simulation, in hardware-in-the-loop testing, and in flight data.
Research and prototype advanced AI and ML methods within perception and estimation, and help mature the ones that prove out into the flight pipeline.
Skills We're Hiring For
Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Math, Physics, or a related field; Master of Science (M.S.) or Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) preferred.
5 to 7 years of experience in applied computer vision, perception, or estimation on real sensor data.
Fluency in state estimation: the Kalman filter family, including nonlinear variants and interacting multiple model (IMM) approaches, applied with judgment.
Data association at multi-target scale: joint probabilistic data association (JPDA), multiple hypothesis tracking, or modern equivalents, chosen with judgment.
Classical optical image and signal processing as a working toolkit, with emphasis on methods for optical sensors: spatial and temporal filtering, morphology, non-uniformity and fixed-pattern noise handling, and techniques for imagery with a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Statistical rigor as a habit: normalized estimation error squared (NEES) and normalized innovation squared (NIS) consistency testing, covariance validation, and calibrated confidence.
3+ years of experience using python to create, alter, and maintain libraries of algorithms within a modern Git & CI/CD framework.
Bonus Points For
Rust for real-time implementation and familiarity with embedded CUDA
Missile, interceptor, or guided-munition perception or tracking experience.
Track-before-detect or other methods for detection and tracking at low SNR.
IR or other non-visible-band sensor experience, including synthetic-to-real domain adaptation.
TensorRT or comparable edge inference deployment experience.
Multi-sensor registration, boresight exploitation, or radar measurement familiarity.
Modern machine learning fluency (PyTorch or equivalent): training, evaluating, and shrinking perception models with measured accuracy tradeoffs.
Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code or similar) to multiply your output.
Eligibility & Logistics
Location: On-site at our Los Angeles, CA HQ; remote work is not available. Monthly weekend travel for test events and supplier engagements. Clearance: A clearance is not required for this position. Must be a U.S. Person

We are seeking an experienced Embedded Systems Engineer III to design, develop, and validate firmware and embedded hardware for real-time products. Experience designing electrical schematics and control panels; familiarity with CAD/Electrical design tools and creating BOMs.

We are a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, we create what is next by pioneering ideas, acting fast, and moving further because standing still just is not in our DNA.

We build software for the world's most ambitious brands, and we're opinionated about how it gets made:
Code quality is a top priority. Style guides, code reviews, and best practices are how we move fast without breaking things. You'll also get your hands on a wide range of cutting-edge technology.

Integrate third-party APIs and systems, and design the contracts that frontend teams and other services build against.

Advocate for best practices in testing, security, performance, and CI/CD, and encourage others to do the same.
Work directly with working-level client stakeholders over email, on calls, and in person, and start building demo and presentation content of your own.
Apply AI and agentic capabilities to real client work, and contribute back to how the craft adopts them through reusable templates, prototyping sessions, and practical guidance for other teams.
Share what you learn, internally through Slack, brown bags, and DEPT U, and externally through articles or talks as project work allows.

Proven experience building and maintaining production-level backend systems used by real people.
Strong proficiency in Python.
Experience designing and integrating APIs and third-party systems.
Solid working knowledge of database platforms, both SQL and NoSQL.
Enough familiarity with modern frontend development (preferably Angular and Typescript) to read the code, review a PR, and debug across the stack.
Experience with at least one major cloud provider. Google Cloud preferred, AWS or Azure also welcome.
Daily, real-world use of GenAI productivity tools (Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex) in your development workflow.
A working understanding of core LLM concepts and where they're a good fit for a problem.
Fluency with version control (git), Agile processes, and CI/CD tooling.
The ability to research independently and know when to ask for help, without spinning wheels on already-solved problems.
A track record of "getting sh*t done" in a fast-paced environment.

Experience mentoring engineers earlier in their careers.
Exposure to agent development frameworks.
Contributions to open source, technical writing, or conference speaking.

As the story goes, in 1949 Frank McNamara finished dinner at a New York restaurant and found he'd left his wallet in another suit. His fix was a card that let members eat now and pay later. That card became Diners Club, widely credited as the first multipurpose charge card. It was a piece of cardboard and a promise: the restaurant trusted the card, the card trusted the member, and someone had to make sure the money actually moved.
More than seventy-five years later, the promise hasn't changed, but the machinery has. When a Mercury customer taps their card, the request goes from the merchant's terminal through an acquirer and a card network to us. In a fraction of a second, we check the balance, apply the customer's spend controls, screen for fraud and say yes or no. After that comes clearing, settlement, disputes and reporting, and every cent has to reconcile.
Cards
are
the way Mercury customers spend money. The Cards Integration team owns the whole Mercury card, not just the swipe: issuance, physical card shipping, spend controls, lifecycle management, authorization, money movement, settlement and reporting, and the infrastructure underneath. We're a full-stack team, and our job is to make the Mercury Debit and IO cards reliable, correct, useful, and innovative.

Description
Training and running large AI models takes enormous amounts of expensive accelerated compute, and most of it sits idle. Across the industry, a large share of GPU capacity is paid for but never does useful work because jobs cannot find it, cannot share it, or cannot see it and use it efficiently. We build the services that closes that gap.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build the systems that put idle or inefficiently used GPUs to work. You will design and build distributed backend services that let organizations pool capacity across many clusters and accounts, route it to the workloads that need it most, and see exactly how it is being used. This is deep systems work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, container orchestration, and cloud infrastructure, and it directly changes how much value customers get from every GPU they pay for.
You will own services end to end, from design through launch and operation in production, and your work will ship to some of the largest AI compute customers in the world.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate distributed backend services that manage and share accelerated compute across multiple clusters and accounts.
Build scheduling and capacity-sharing capabilities that move compute to the highest-priority workloads and reclaim it when priorities change.
Build zero-touch usage and guidance systems that collect, aggregate, and report how compute is consumed, at scale and in near real time.
Own your services in production: define operational metrics, respond to issues, and continuously improve reliability, latency, and cost.
Write clear design documents, participate in design and code reviews, and raise the engineering bar for the team.
Collaborate with product, design, and partner engineering teams to turn customer problems into shipped features.
Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of ownership, quality, and customer focus.
A day in the life
Most days start with a short team stand-up, then it is mostly building. You might design a service that lets one cluster borrow idle capacity from another, then write it up for a design review where the team pokes holes in it before any code is written. Hard problems get their own deep-dive whiteboard session. Other days lean toward operations, chasing down why a workload did not get the capacity it should have. You will not be handed fully specified tasks; you will have the independence to help decide what to build, then build it.
About The Team
We help customers get the most out of the accelerated compute they pay for. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure every accelerator a customer pays for is doing useful work, and make that easy to see and control. Cost reduction is one important part of that, but the bigger idea is the engine that delivers compute to the workloads that need it most, in as little time as possible.
Our customers run some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world, and they feel the impact of our work directly in how much they can do with their infrastructure. We care about depth, we own our work end to end, and we build in the open where we can.

Experience programming with at least one software programming language

What You'll Do
The Instrumentation & Controls (I&C) engineer/tech will be responsible for developing high quality detailed design packages, providing engineering procurement and field technical support to implement those designs, and providing expertise for troubleshooting and technical assessments of plant systems. Design involves the preparation of conceptual engineering deliverables such as cost-estimating bills of material and labor-hour estimates, statements of work, design criteria, and required design output deliverables. Design output deliverables include conduit/cable schedules, conduit/equipment plans, wiring/connection/schematic diagrams, instrument loop diagrams, various sections/elevations/detail drawings, calculations, instrument datasheets, and construction specifications.
I&C engineer/tech will apply technical expertise and wide application of technical principles, theories and concepts in the electrical engineering field with primarily an instrumentation/controls focus for process measurement and control. I&C engineer/tech will develop industrial control panel assembly drawings, control system network architecture diagrams, and control logic for both batch and continuous processes using conventional analog instrumentation, modern digital control systems, and programmable logic controller/human-machine interfaces (PLCs/HMIs). I&C engineer/tech will also develop process control system narratives, aid in the development of process software requirements, and provide input to Process and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs).
The I&C engineer/tech will provide self-performed technical solutions to a wide range of problems through the application of established engineering practices and national consensus codes and standards. Candidate must effectively and cooperatively work as a team member of a multi-discipline, integrated project team. The I&C engineer/tech will routinely perform walkdowns in the existing plant facilities in order to generate design documents and provide field support to craft personnel.

Susquehanna is looking for a Virtualization Engineer to help design and build infrastructure for our trading platforms on OpenStack. You will work closely with other infrastructure engineers and software developers to create scalable systems.

Automate and Evolve:
Contribute to our library of home-grown tools, written primarily in Python and Bash, utilizing tools such as Jenkins to automate bare-metal and virtual server deployments, monitoring, and maintenance, allowing you to focus on performance related issues and projects.

Create:
Design and implement our next-generation VM platform in OpenStack which is slated to replace our 18000 guest VMWare environment.

A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
1-5 years of progressive experience building Linux based platforms at scale.

Recent hands-on experience with automation in Python, required
In-depth experience in open-source-based virtualization such as OpenStack, RedHat Openshift, kubevirt, or similar.

Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm founded by a group of friends who share a passion for game theory and probabilistic thinking. From offices around the world, our employees collaborate to make optimal decisions and are driven by the desire to achieve winning results together.

We are experts in trading essentially all listed financial products and asset classes, with a focus on derivatives trading. We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.
Role Mission
Mid-training sits at the seam between pre-training and post-training and is one of the highest-leverage points in the entire model pipeline. This is where raw base model capability is sharpened into something that can reason deeply, generalize reliably, and serve as the foundation that post-training builds on.
You will own the late-stage training decisions that determine what our models are fundamentally capable of: data mix and quality uplift, annealing schedules, context length extension, capability injection across coding, math, and reasoning, and the synthetic data strategies that make all of it scale. This role does cross-cutting work across what is classically considered both pre-training and post-training. We don't distinguish between research and engineering; we expect both.
What You'll Accomplish
Data Mix and Quality Uplift: Design and iterate on high-quality data mixtures for late-stage and annealing training runs. Develop principled methods for sourcing, filtering, and weighting data to sharpen model capabilities without degrading general performance.
Capability Injection: Drive targeted improvements in coding, mathematics, and long-horizon reasoning through curated data strategies and training interventions. Translate research insights into measurable capability gains on our agents.
Synthetic Data Research: Develop and evaluate synthetic data pipelines that generate training signal at scale. Understand the limits and failure modes of synthetic approaches and build methods that hold up in production training runs.

Strong proficiency in SIMULINK programming and STK, with familiarity in C, C++, Python, and version control tools such as GIT/SVN.
Fundamental knowledge of GNC algorithms and experience with designing at least one of guidance, navigation, control, or FDIR algorithms.
Understanding of the working principles of IMUs, GPS, star trackers, RCS, non-propulsive actuators (Reaction Wheels, Magnetic Torquer Bars, Control Moment Gyros), and LIDAR.

Strong fundamental knowledge of dynamic modeling, control, guidance, or navigation algorithm design, state-space systems, SISO, and MIMO systems.
Ability to estimate workload independently and accurately on short-term tasks, including JIRA tickets.
Experience running Monte Carlo simulations and performing in-depth analysis to troubleshoot and optimize GNC systems.
Strong understanding of autonomous GNC mode transitions and ability to perform relevant analysis.
Familiarity with SIMULINK autocoding and Linux systems for simulation and software integration.
Ability to take ownership of performance requirements and conduct detailed analysis to ensure compliance.
Experience working with GNC flight software in target test simulation environments and conducting validation testing.
Knowledge of spacecraft subsystems, including power and thermal systems, communication antennas, and control structure interaction principles.

About AIUC
AIUC builds standards and insurance for frontier AI. Our mission is to Underwrite superintelligence. We exist because risk, not capability, is becoming the binding constraint on AI being useful. History offers lessons for how to build confidence in new technology; electricity burned down houses until insurers funded Underwriters Laboratories (UL) to certify products against their standards. Today, the UL mark is a trustmark on every light bulb in America. We’re building that for AI.
AIUC-1, our standard for agent security, serves frontier builders like Cursor, Lovable, ElevenLabs, and Harvey. We've raised $55m from Ribbit, First Harmonic and Nat Friedman to audit frontier AI. Our team comes from METR, Anthropic, McKinsey, and OpenAI. Come join us.
The Role
Every AI company that comes to us wants the same thing: proof their agent is safe enough to sell to an enterprise. Getting there means running thousands of evaluations against their live system.
We've now certified the category leaders in every major AI vertical: ElevenLabs (voice), Intercom (customer service), UiPath (workflow automation), Lovable (coding), and more we'll announce soon. No two of those systems look alike: each has its own authentication, its own interface, its own definition of what a failure even looks like. Before we can test any of it, someone has to sit with that customer, understand how their agent actually works, and get it wired into our evaluation system.
We're hiring an
engineer to own that work end to end
. You'll have your own set of customers within your first weeks, paired with a commercial counterpart on each one.
In This Role, You Will
Own the path from signed customer to delivered results - scoping what to test, working through their authentication and interfaces, and getting their agent running in our system
Build the one-off version when a customer doesn't fit the product yet, and make it work anyway
Deliver results directly to the customer and be the person they trust with the technical detail
Make the call on whether a customer meets the AIUC-1 standard
Work across the widest surface of any role here: our Delivery team, our core engineers, sales, the Standards team (shaping what goes into AIUC-1), and your customer's own engineering team
Turn what you learn in the field into the product
That last one is why the role exists. We're building toward a product that runs evaluations end to end without an engineer in the loop. This is a high-agency role: you'll shape what we build next as much as you'll deliver what we've built.
If you're planning to start a company one day, this is a front row seat. You'll work directly with our founders, with founders at the companies we certify, and alongside a team full of ex-founders.
What We're Looking For
The job in practice looks like reading someone's API docs, chasing credentials, building integrations into customers' systems and agents. Then evaluating whether those agents behave, and owning the failure modes the evals surface. The person who thrives here has done this work before. What drives them is trust and safety.
To Be Successful, We Think You Have
3-7 years of experience, likely as an early engineer at a startup where you ended up owning customers, or in an integration, solutions, or forward deployed role selling technical products to technical buyers. (Impact matters more than years.)
Enough software engineering to build and debug an integration yourself, and the judgment to know when the scrappy version is the right answer
Comfort owning a customer relationship directly – scoping the work, setting expectations, and delivering bad news early
Customer obsession: their problem is your problem, and you see it through
The discipline to turn what you see in the field into something reusable rather than solving the same problem twice
Nice to have
Experience founding or co-founding a company
Experience with AI evaluations or red-teaming
Executive presence with senior stakeholders
Our Values
We are in the business of building trust. We take our values seriously and treat them as commitments to each other, held to the same bar as the ones we make to customers.
Strong back: high standards, keep our promises, work hard.
Fast feet: experiment, cut scope, take delight in pace.
Eyes up: wrestle with the mission, and let where AI is heading shape our strategy, our teams and our day-to-day work.
Open heart: say the scary thing, create connection, make room for emotions.
Underwriting superintelligence is our life's work. If you want it to be yours, apply now.

Competitive annual salary
Equity (significant part of total compensation)
Health, dental and vision insurance for you and your dependents
Visa sponsorship and relocation stipend to bring you to SF, if needed
Daily lunch, dinner & snacks

Lightmatter builds chips that enable extreme-scale artificial intelligence computing clusters. Join a multidisciplinary team to pioneer the future of computing by building the world's most advanced communications lasers. In this role you will help build the control plane and diagnostics software behind next-generation photonic interconnect products - implementing laser control and stabilization routines, the telemetry and monitoring firmware that keeps them healthy in the field, and the tooling that brings new hardware to life. You will work shoulder-to-shoulder with photonic, analog, digital, and systems engineers, own well-defined pieces of the stack end to end, and grow your depth in a domain where very few engineers have experience. Your work will be visible in every product we ship.
Responsibilities
Implement and tune active laser control and stabilization algorithms on embedded targets, working from architecture and control approaches defined with the cross-functional design team.
Own delivery of well-scoped firmware components for photonic transceiver diagnostics, telemetry, and monitoring; from requirements through bring-up, test, and release.
Contribute to control plane and diagnostics architecture discussions across a multidisciplinary team of photonic, analog, digital, systems, and network engineers.
Integrate transceiver management and telemetry with data center administration interfaces such as CMIS, OpenBMC, and DMTF standards.
Bring up new hardware alongside hardware engineers, and debug embedded systems using GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, and oscilloscopes.
Characterize and debug laser behavior using optical test and measurement equipment, and build the automated test and data collection scripts that make that work repeatable.
Adapt existing practices where they fit and devise new approaches where precedent is limited, working independently with review at critical checkpoints.
Write clear documentation and share findings with engineers outside your specialty, adapting how you communicate to the audience.
Qualifications
BS and 5+ years of experience, MS and 3+ years of experience, or a PhD; equivalent practical experience also considered.
Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field.
Experience contributing embedded software to a product that shipped to customers, or to hardware that reached production or field deployment.
Proficiency in C or C++, and comfort with Python for tooling, test, and analysis.
Solid understanding of hardware-software integration, including common embedded peripherals and buses (I2C, SPI, UART, GPIO).
Experience developing firmware in resource constrained environments; experience in both bare-metal and RTOS systems preferred. FreeRTOS, Zephyr or other modern RTOS experience preferred.
Hands-on lab experience debugging embedded systems with GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, or oscilloscopes.
Working knowledge of Git, and experience with CMake or a comparable build system.
Demonstrated ability to take ownership of a defined problem, work through ambiguity, and deliver on commitments in a fast-moving environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Coursework, research, or industry experience in closed-loop control: designing, simulating, or deploying control algorithms on real systems.
Experience developing firmware for optical transceivers, photonic systems, or other precision analog/mixed-signal hardware.
Familiarity with CMIS, OpenBMC, DMTF/Redfish, or similar platform management environments.
Exposure to optical communication systems, laser physics, or thermal and wavelength stabilization techniques.
Familiarity with optical test and measurement, and with methodologies for characterizing optical components and systems.
Experience building test automation, hardware-in-the-loop test benches, or CI for firmware.
A track record of learning unfamiliar technical domains quickly and becoming the person teammates come to with questions.
